advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard emit_code_workspace_state so a failed/short `git rev-list` produces an explicit error rather than an 'ahead , behind ' diagnostic that looks like a real measurement.
evidence: ABSENCE: no check that code_workspace_distance succeeded or produced two fields before emitting the drift diagnostic
advisory.finding: emit_code_workspace_state parses `code_workspace_distance` output with `set -- $distance` and blindly reads $1/$2; if rev-list emits fewer than two fields (e.g. it errored, or origin/main is not resolvable) `ahead`/`behind` become empty and the log line reads 'ahead , behind ', a malformed drift signal indistinguishable from a real measurement. The distance/SHA producers are never checked for success before their output is trusted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture the rev-list rc and field count; if the command failed or did not yield exactly two integers, emit an explicit 'could not measure drift' error instead of a partially-blank line.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Serialize the entrypoint's `merge --ff-only` working-tree write against concurrent `source=local` gate reads of MCP_CODE_DIR (a shared lock the Python server also honors), or document that local-mode reads are unsafe during startup refresh.
evidence: Writer (new): `if ! git -C "${MCP_CODE_DIR}" merge --ff-only origin/main; then` — mcp-entrypoint.sh:189 mutates refs/heads/main, the index, and working-tree files; the prior present-checkout path did NOT write (clone_code_locked/provision_code returned 0 when code_repo_present).
Executor 1: `provision_store &` runs the refresh in the background — mcp-entrypoint.sh:281.

Executor 2: `exec "$@"` starts `rebar-mcp` concurrently — mcp-entrypoint.sh:282; the server serves gates on worker threads (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:398 'so certified-op instrumentation can gauge worker-thread calls').

Shared-resource reader: `source=local` is a client-supplied per-request arg (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:350-351, 377-378) and reads the in-place checkout working tree directly — docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md:15 'read the server's in-place checkout directly (uncommitted/dirty content allowed)'.

Sibling accessor + its guard: the write is guarded by `with_dir_lock "$code_dir" "code checkout" refresh_code_locked` (mcp-entrypoint.sh:173) whose `flock -w "$MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_WAIT" 9` (mcp-entrypoint.sh:73-74) locks only the MCP_CODE_DIR inode among shell entrypoint peers; the Python server never takes that flock, so the local-mode working-tree read is the unlocked twin.

Attested path is NOT racy (guard verified): docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md:48 'REBAR_ROOT only locates the object DB'; attested mode materializes an immutable pinned snapshot at a resolved SHA (repo_snapshot.py:1-8), so a fast-forward that only appends objects + atomically moves refs cannot corrupt a concurrent origin/main resolution.

Harm: a local-mode gate reading the working tree during the fast-forward observes a mix of pre- and post-merge file contents (a torn tree), producing an incorrect / non-reproducible review verdict — the exact non-reproducibility the snapshot design (docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md:3) exists to avoid.
advisory.finding: The startup refresh's `git merge --ff-only origin/main` write to the MCP_CODE_DIR working tree can interleave with a concurrent `source=local` gate read of that same working tree, because the entrypoint's inode flock is not held by the MCP server process — yielding a torn tree and a wrong/non-reproducible local-mode verdict.
scenarios: Container (re)start: the once-per-boot background refresh_code performs merge --ff-only while an early client issues a review_code/scan_spec/verify_completion request with source=local against the same server.

evidence: Shared resource: refs/remotes/origin/main in the common git dir of MCP_CODE_DIR (== REBAR_ROOT == /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code, docker-compose.yml:501-502).
Executor A (new writer): `provision_store &` at mcp-entrypoint.sh:281 -> provision_code (mcp-entrypoint.sh:220 refresh_code) -> refresh_code_locked `git fetch origin main` at mcp-entrypoint.sh:184.

Executor B (concurrent reader/fetcher): `exec "$@"` at mcp-entrypoint.sh:282 launches the MCP server; its attested gates call repo_snapshot.resolve_ref -> fetch_origin at src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:204.

Sibling accessor + its guard: fetch_origin serializes ref-updating fetches under fetch_coordination_lock keyed on the git COMMON dir (src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py:311-325, `_FETCH_COORD_LOCK_NAME`).

Documented harm from the sibling itself: src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py:237-240 — 'Two uncoordinated ref-updating fetches against one common dir race git's ref compare-and-swap, and the loser fails `cannot lock ref '<ref>': is at <new> but expected <old>` — the snapshot fetch aborts an attested op.'

ABSENCE rationale: the with_dir_lock the entrypoint holds (mcp-entrypoint.sh:73, `exec 9<"$wdl_dir"`) is an flock on the DIRECTORY inode /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code, a different lock file from <common>/fetch-coord lock; the gate reader never acquires the directory-inode lock, so the guard does not prevent the ref-CAS interleaving.
advisory.finding: The entrypoint's new `refresh_code_locked` runs `git fetch origin main` as raw git without taking rebar's common-dir fetch coordination lock, so it can race the concurrently-running MCP server's attested-gate fetch on refs/remotes/origin/main and cause the gate's fetch to abort with a 'cannot lock ref' ref-CAS failure.

evidence: ABSENCE: no guard that `$distance` actually contains two numeric fields before echoing them; a failed/empty rev-list yields a diagnostic indistinguishable from a genuine 'ahead , behind ' with blanks
advisory.finding: emit_code_workspace_state parses distance with `set -- $distance` and reads $1/$2 without checking that two fields were produced; if `git rev-list ... HEAD...origin/main` emits nothing (e.g. origin/main missing or the rev-list errors) the diagnostic prints empty ahead/behind values ('ahead , behind '), and the SHA capture / distance capture failures are swallowed by command substitution so a broken instrument silently degrades the diagnostic instead of signaling.

evidence: 190:     echo "mcp: diverged code checkout — refusing to refresh" >&2
advisory.finding: A workspace whose local HEAD is AHEAD of origin/main (e.g. origin/main force-pushed backward, or a stray local commit reachable-clean) will pass the dirty check and the fetch, then fail `merge --ff-only` and be reported as 'diverged code checkout'. The ahead-only case is not truly diverged; the label mis-describes the condition an operator sees, though the safe no-mutation posture is preserved.

provision_code now propagates refresh failure into rc (`refresh_code; return $?`), so a dirty/diverged/unreachable present checkout makes provision_store return non-zero where it previously returned 0 for any present checkout. In --provision-only mode this flips exit status to 1; in normal startup provisioning is backgrounded so the container still starts. This behavior change is intended per the ticket's 'fail loud' posture but any caller/health check keying on provision_store's exit code for an otherwise-healthy present checkout now sees failures on drift refusal.
